audit.evidence: REAL Apache OFBiz built from source per release18.12 commit (base eclipse-temurin:8-jdk-jammy, gradle 5.0-rc-5, seed data loaded into embedded Derby); the auth guard is the REAL org.apache.ofbiz.webapp.control.LoginWorker.checkLogin() reached by an EXTERNAL HTTPS request to the real ControlServlet. NO OFBiz source copied or modified; a benign authz-canary webapp (plugins/pcbcanary) adds one <security auth="true"/> request whose groovy event echoes ${PCB_FLAG} iff checkLogin returns "success". Gate via `python3 oracle.py --run-gate` on real Docker: residual GET /pcbcanary/control/flag?USERNAME=Y&PASSWORD=Y&requirePasswordChange=Y -> 200 + FLAG on v1 (18.12.10), login/error page + NO flag on v2 (18.12.11); seed /webtools/control/xmlrpc -> resolves on v0, 'Unknown request [xmlrpc]' on v1. passed=true. Positive controls: no-auth /pcbcanary/control/flag -> login page/no flag on v1; residual also reaches flag on v0 (bypass predates 49070).

root_cause: Authentication bypass: LoginWorker.login() returns 'requirePasswordChange' (not 'error') on a failed userLogin when requirePasswordChange=Y, so checkLogin()'s guard falls through to 'success' for non-empty invalid credentials (auth bypass / CWE-306)

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: CVE-2023-49070 was fixed in 18.12.10 by REMOVING the pre-auth XML-RPC deserialization endpoint, but the underlying authentication bypass was left untouched. In LoginWorker.login(), a failed userLogin service call with requirePasswordChange=Y returned "requirePasswordChange" instead of "error"; checkLogin() only blocks when login() returns "error", so a request with non-empty invalid USERNAME/PASSWORD and requirePasswordChange=Y falls through to "success" and reaches protected endpoints unauthenticated. CVE-2023-51467 (18.12.11, OFBIZ-12873, commit 1dcfa071804a) changed the failure return to "error" (and hardened null checks to UtilValidate.isEmpty()).
